articles.title: Volkanovski vs Evloev Breakdown: Can the Champ Stop an Undefeated Wrestler? | UFC 333
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski defends the UFC featherweight title against undefeated Movsar Evloev (20-0) in the UFC 333 main event Saturday, October 24 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. Volkanovski came back from two losses to Islam Makhachev and a knockout loss to Ilia Topuria to beat Diego Lopes twice, first for the vacant title at UFC 314 and again in Sydney at UFC 325. Evloev earned his shot with a majority decision over Lerone Murphy in a title eliminator in March. Only seven of his 20 wins are finishes. Can Evloev get the champion down and keep him there? Volk says he’s keeping it on the feet. articles.title: Josh Hokit is one win away from becoming the biggest star in MMA
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is not ready to let the Bruce Buffer and Josh Hokit thing go, and he wants to be clear about why: this is not against Bruce, who he calls awesome and a friend. He is discussing the topic Bruce brought up, the idea that the way Hokit speaks is somehow the problem. Chael's case starts with the stakes. Josh Hokit is one win away from being the biggest star in MMA, and that win would make him the first undefeated, undisputed heavyweight champion the sport has ever had. Then comes the question that proves the point: could Hokit outdraw Sean O'Malley, Alex Pereira, Ilia Topuria or Justin Gaethje right now? Nobody is sure, and the fact that nobody is sure is the answer. Those men are world champions and former champions. Hokit is neither. He is the undefeated number one contender about to sell out Madison Square Garden, and he is already in that conversation. From there Chael turns Bruce's comment inside out with the laws of logic. If the way Josh speaks is wrong, the opposite has to be right, and the opposite is dead silence: no press conferences, no interviews, no need for Joe Rogan at all. Or he could speak like everybody else, and Chael performs that version too, the safe answer that thanks everybody and says nothing. Nobody wants either version. When you speak to Hokit you get the different sides of him instead, and when he is about to talk, people in living rooms and bars go quiet to hear him. Chael says he has only witnessed that twice before, with Rampage Jackson and then Conor McGregor. The UFC follows a code, the same code that never shut Sean Strickland out of a single media opportunity, and Chael says that code will be extended to Hokit. Subscribe for more from Chael Sonnen and tell us in the comments: should Hokit change how he talks, or is that exactly why everybody stops to listen? articles.title: Floyd vs Conor 2, Who Writes the Check?
articles.description: Floyd Mayweather is talking about Conor McGregor again, and Chael Sonnen says the whole situation feels very different this time. Chael shares what Conor told him personally when he asked him about Floyd during a fight week: anytime Conor thinks of Floyd, he just sees dollar signs. From there, Chael breaks down how Pretty Boy Floyd was not a star before 2005, how the Money Mayweather gimmick, the watches, the cash, and the rap-video presentation, is what actually made people care, and why that same gimmick lands very differently when you are publicly calling for a fight because you need the money. He also questions the money stories the pundits repeated for years, including the Forbes highest-paid-athlete claims, and asks a simple question nobody in the room could answer on one of the biggest podcasts in the world: if Floyd was paid $100 million to fight Conor, who wrote the check? Then Chael turns to Floyd himself. Boxing only exists because somebody is willing to lose a lot of money to be tied to the tough guy business, and the man who wrote that check took his beating and got out. The Money Team, presented alongside Showtime Sports as a real promotion, is little more than a form filed through Ogden, Utah, the same empty co-promote trick Fedor's M-1 tried with the UFC. Floyd already controls half the fight just by making the walk. The problem is the spread: Conor did not get paid what he claims, Floyd knows the made-up number, and he cannot cover it. So why would anyone else step in and take the same loss Floyd will not take himself? Subscribe for more from Chael Sonnen and tell us in the comments: does Floyd vs. Conor 2 ever actually happen? articles.title: Bo Nickal Called It
articles.description: Bo Nickal warned Gable Steveson to his face, and a few weeks later Gable got knocked out. Chael Sonnen was backstage when the warning happened, and he says Bo's whole point now is simple: I told you so. Chael breaks down a feud he admits he found out about late. Bo Nickal and Gable Steveson, both wrestlers, had gone at each other in the media, and Bo confronted Gable backstage at a Real American Freestyle event. Bo's stance was that wrestlers should prop each other up instead of tearing each other down. But his fight take was blunt: Gable is the bigger wrestler and likely beats him in a wrestling match, yet in a fight Gable does not have the reactions or the defenses for strikes yet, and Bo would be able to hit him standing. Then Gable got caught and knocked out, which Chael says proves Bo's premise. From there Chael turns it into a bigger question: is Gable Steveson a heel, does he want to be one, and could it work if he is not willing to live with the boos? A real heel, Chael says, loves the boos, the thumbs down and the middle fingers, because that is the public telling him he is doing his job. Having no opinion about you at all is the road to poverty in this business. And there is a third option that only happens by accident, the cool heel: Chael tells the Stone Cold Steve Austin story, and the Jon Jones press conference moment opposite Daniel Cormier, when Jones said the line he never wanted to say out loud, braced for the crowd to turn on him, and they went crazy for him instead. So what happens if Gable goes heel: do they support him, reject him, or make him extremely monetizable as a cool heel? articles.title: Islam vs Prates Is Not Even Close to Done
articles.description: Islam Makhachev vs Carlos Prates is not done. In fact, Chael Sonnen says it is not even close to done, and that is coming from Rizvan, a straight shooter who does not do marketing and does not say things for attention. Rizvan did not explain what he meant, only that negotiations are underway and his definition of done is simple: two guys have agreed to meet at a specific date in a specific location, and that has not happened. Chael agrees with that definition, then asks the obvious question. The weight class is known, the contracts are signed, and the UFC already holds both men's schedules, passports, hotels and glove sizes. So what is the holdup? Chael's guess is that it is not money. Rizvan, Ali Abdelaziz, Khabib and Islam's camp have never played that game, and it was put to the test when Islam lost Arman Tsarukyan and accepted Renato Moicano on 31 hours' notice. So it is not for sure Prates. A month ago, with inside information, Chael believed it was going to be Michael Morales. Then Ian Garry played it masterfully by going after Morales, and Shavkat Rakhmonov popped up and went after Morales too, selling an undefeated vs undefeated fight. Both men went after Morales for the same reason: everybody understood Morales is next, so beating him takes his spot. Morales accepted both callouts, but nobody fanned those flames, no press conference, no announcement while it was red hot. Chael reads that as a clue those fights were never the plan. Meanwhile Prates has no other idea and nobody is calling him out, so Islam and Prates look like the two just left on the board. And now Rizvan says that fight is far from done, which means Morales is still in play. But Morales did nothing: the Garry and Rakhmonov ideas started with Garry and Rakhmonov, not with him. If Morales believes the shot is his, he needs to make a move, and Chael will follow his lead. Right now, there is nothing to go off of. The only guy tying himself to Islam is Prates. We need to hear from Morales. Subscribe for more from Chael Sonnen and tell us in the comments: who should Islam Makhachev fight next? articles.title: An Undefeated UFC Fighter Just Learned a Harsh Lesson #ufc
articles.description: An undefeated fighter with a 16-0 record and a 7-0 UFC run gets released — and Chael Sonnen says there's a bigger message here for every fighter on the roster. Chael admits he didn't even know who the fighter was before the release. But he isn't criticizing the fighter for that. Instead, he questions whether the old rules of the UFC are changing. But what happens if that is no longer enough? Chael believes this release could be a warning to the entire roster: success inside the Octagon may not guarantee job security anymore. Is the UFC changing what it values in its fighters, or has this always been part of the business?
